newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Cement may stop T$80 bln project.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Cement may stop T$80 bln project.

text.p: Taiwan Cement said on Thursday it may halt an T$80 billion cement investment in eastern Hualien in a dispite with the government over mine exploration rights in western Taiwan.
"If the economics ministry fails to keep its vow to end all mine exploration rights in western Taiwan, we may stop our T$80 billion Hualien project," a company spokeswoman told Reuters.
The ministry has promised to end all cement makers' mine exploration rights in western Taiwan by the end of 1997 and had urged local makers to move their plants to eastern Taiwan.
The strategy aimed to boost eastern Taiwan's lagging economy, but had sparked complaints from environmentalists.
Eastern Taiwan's higher production costs have made most makers hesitant to move. Only Taiwan Cement followed the policy and did so, leaving it at a competitive disadvantage.
"Now we hear that the economics ministry plans to extend mine exploration rights in western Taiwan. This move is unfair to Taiwan Cement," the spokeswoman said.
Taiwan Cement has spelled out its concerns in a complaint to the ministry, threatening to halt the Hualien project if the government goes ahead with the policy reversal.
"We have sent the ministry a letter asking it to make it clear that it won't extend the (western Taiwan) rights or else we will have to close the T$80 billion project," she said.
An economics ministry spokesman confirmed that the policy was under review but that no final decision had been made.
"We will make a cautious assessment," ministry spokesman Teng Song-tang told Reuters. "We've made no final decision."
Taiwan Cement had planned to build a cement factory, a power plant and an industrial harbour in the state-sponsored Hoping cement zone in Hualien.
In December 1995, the firm said it was suspending the T$80 billion investment project because of serious environmental protection protests there.
Since the environmental protests eased in late 1996, the company has gradually relaunched the project.
"So far, we have invested T$2 billion in preparatory works in the project," the Taiwan Cement spokeswoman said.
